bibl.title: The Greek and Roman Ports of the Red Sea Coast in the Eastern Desert of Egypt.
bibl.seg: Doaa Fadel, The Greek and Roman Ports of the Red Sea Coast in the Eastern Desert of Egypt.
International Journal of Heritage, Tourism and Hospitality 11 (2017) No. 4, pp. 229-258, figg.
bibl.note: Introduction. - Methodology. First: Geography of the Eastern Desert. - Second: The history and importance of the Eastern Desert through Greek and Roman period. - Third: The ports of the Red Sea coast through Greek and Roman period. - The ports of the Red Sea Coast. (I) Arsinoe Port. - Red Sea canal. - Importance of the Red Sea canal. - Location of Red sea canal. - The course of Red Sea canal. - (II) Abu Sha'r Port. - Abu Sha'r's road. - Abu Sha'r's fort. - (III) Philotera / Aenum Port. - (IV) Nechesia / Marsa Nakari Port. - The excavations and the archaeological remains of Nechesia / Marsa Nakari Port. - (V) Berenike Port. - (I) Berenike-Apollonopolis Magna (Edfu) Road. - (II) Berenike-Coptos (Quft) Road. - The excavations and the archaeological remains of Berenike Port. - (VI) Myos Hormos "Quseir el-Qadim" Port. - The excavations and thearchaeological remains of Myos Hormos Port.
